title: bug: a candidate-caused dependency-phase refusal (supervisor exit 81) is infra-failure, so the daemon retries it on fresh VMs and escalates with an empty output tail
description: guest-supervisor.py exits 81 for every dependency-phase failure: npm ci out of sync with the protected lockfile, and since CQ-R13 a planted npm-shrinkwrap.json/.npmrc or a missing package.json. npm's output goes to /dev/null, check-session.mjs maps 81 to infra-failure, and packages/moe-daemon/src/delivery/repairPolicy.ts retries infra failures, so a candidate that breaks its own install burns the infra retry budget on fresh VMs and the worker never sees why. Split candidate-caused install refusals into a code-failure outcome with a bounded output tail, apart from VM and toolchain faults.
definitionOfDone: A dependency-phase refusal caused by the candidate's files resolves as code-failure with a bounded, sanitized output tail, and is not retried as infra.
A toolchain, cache or VM fault in the same phase stays infra-failure; tests cover both through check-session and the daemon's repair policy.

implementationPlan.description:

Let actual runCheckSession consume the Python child's clean no-frame exit. Table-drive candidate metadata refusal => exactly {outcome:'code-failure', exitCode:82, signal:null, outputTail:<the fixed host diagnostic>}; missing toolchain/cache error/unknown npm exit => infra-failure, never candidate; timeout retains its existing timeout/infra distinction. Assert zero check-command marker and no npm installation on rejected metadata. Plant CR/LF, ANSI, secrets and long/unicode strings in candidate fields/stderr and assert outputTail is the same host-owned ASCII literal, <=512 UTF8 bytes, with none of those inputs. Track only owned child PIDs, clean them and temp dirs, require Linux/WSL execution rather than a skipped native-Windows row.

In packages/moe-daemon/src/delivery/repairPolicy.test.ts import runCheckSession from '../../../../scripts/local-runner/check-session.mjs' (test-only, never production import). Use an EventEmitter child plus Writable stdin and PassThrough stdout/stderr, following the scripts test's checkProvider event order: write callback completes, stdout ends, then close 82 or 81. Pass the resulting outcome/nonzero exitCode/outputTail into the existing run()/decide()/cands() helpers; use the runner convention exitCode ?? 1 only for an infra result with no observed code. Assert the candidate result produces action:'repair', not retry-infra, with the bounded nonempty diagnostic preserved; the infrastructure result produces action:'retry-infra', consumes only maxInfraRetries and retains the existing escalation behavior. A zero infra budget must not prevent the candidate repair. Repeating the same unchanged code failure must never start an infra retry; existing code-repair escalation rules still apply. Do not change repairPolicy.ts or mock its decision. Keep existing C1/I1 tests intact. This parent owns integration/hardening for the split; the broader epic-final native certification stays CQ-R13.

implementationPlan.note:
Ran the adversarial self-review once, over the three-file diff and the check-session.mjs seam. No code changes resulted, so the step-4 gate stands; the sha256s are unchanged (d149aa19… / 48262f6d… / e4a34300…).

Findings:
1. Every 82 comes after holds() (79), reown (65/71) and protect_mounts, and before relay. No frame, no npm, no job. Only reads and lexists run, so no workspace bytes change on a refusal. The root fd is closed in a finally.
2. CandidateDependencyInvalid is a bare Exception, so neither outer handler (ValueError/RecursionError/OSError → 81) catches it. Only check_job's dedicated except maps it to 82.
3. 82 needs a positive candidate cause: package.json ENOENT/ELOOP, ValueError (non-regular, oversized, malformed), RecursionError, a metadata mismatch, UNAPPROVED_CONTROLS, or shrinkwrap/.npmrc. These stay 81: lockfile faults, any other errno, growth/shrink while reading (now an OSError), a malformed list, a missing toolchain, npm failure and timeout.
4. Infra wins across all directories, in either order.
5. Host seam: timeout, then failed/killed/!written/!ended, then 82 only with no frame. 82 can never pass, and its outputTail is the fixed host ASCII text; stderr is never read.

Mutation sweep (scratch, /tmp/moe-42e-mut, `^(KI[1-9]|C[29]) `, scored by exit code): the no-op control passes, and 20/20 mutants are killed. They are: no check_job catch; 81→82; raise at once without the all-dir pass; every OSError → candidate; every OSError → infra; ELOOP dropped; ENOENT dropped; growth → ValueError; bad lock root → candidate; shrinkwrap/.npmrc → infra; constant 83; post-loop raise dropped; package ValueError → infra; RecursionError dropped; lexists check dropped; bad lockfile in loop → candidate; outer except swallowing the candidate; the class subclassing ValueError; controls check dropped; metadata mismatch ignored. In step 3, mutants in check-session.mjs (82→infra, 81→code) were killed by H1-H3. No leftover processes (checked by env marker) and no leftover dirs.

Theoretical, noted only:
(a) If an operator PROTECTS package.json or .npmrc and the approved base already disagrees with its lockfile, the candidate cannot fix it. Repair then escalates through unchanged-failure or the budget.
(b) A dir deleted between the lockfile read and the package.json read gives ENOENT → 82. Nothing runs in the guest at that point.

completionSummary:
A candidate-caused dependency refusal now exits 82 (DEPENDENCIES_CANDIDATE_INVALID) instead of 81. The host maps it to code-failure with a fixed ASCII diagnostic, so decideRepair repairs instead of retrying as infra.

Supervisor (sha256 d149aa19…f18a):
- Gives 82 for the candidate's package.json when it is missing, symlinked, not regular, oversized, not strict JSON, too deep, mismatched with the lockfile root, or carries overrides, bundling or workspaces; also for a planted npm-shrinkwrap.json or .npmrc.
- Keeps 81 for lockfile faults, any other OSError (EACCES, EIO, a file resized while read), a malformed list, a missing toolchain, and npm failure or timeout.
- Checks every directory first, and an 81 cause in any directory outranks an 82.
- Exits 82 before hello: no frame, no npm, no job. Only after the 79/65/71 checks.

Tests:
- local-runner-check: cause-specific KI3/KI5/KI7, KI8 with real npm, new KI9 (precedence and injected errnos), C2 pinning "79 80 81 82", and new C9. C9 runs 12 rows through the real supervisor main() and the real runCheckSession. Hostile stderr (an npm token, CR/LF/ANSI, 0xff bytes) never reaches outputTail.
- repairPolicy.test.ts: new H1-H3 feed real runCheckSession results into the unchanged decideRepair: 82 → repair, 81 → bounded retry-infra then escalate, a repeated 82 → unchanged-failure.

Unchanged: repairPolicy.ts, check-session.mjs and local-runner.test.mjs.
